# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–11 (Complete – Updated 101)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; spring of third year (auction, financial crisis, engagement rupture); military mobilization period following Napoleon's escape and landing; thaw period with frost-silvered hedges and rain threatening, early light of year; summer of third year; evening with wind off water, salt and tar smell, frost silvering hedges overnight, vespers bells, bees in lavender; early autumn with coughing sickness, dog barking, turnips on cart, river up, price of salt concerns; late April: gusty raw day with rain whipping pavement, end of day with early light, smoke flat over fields; church service with rattling rain on windows; autumn of third year (river crossing at Quenwick); Brighton period following George-Amelia marriage (early spring/late April): turnips on cart, threatening rain, wind off water with salt and tar smell, frost-silvered hedges, flat smoke over fields, ruts and puddles after thaw; Dobbin's delayed arrival bringing news of Belgium orders; early light of year returning; **current: evening at Ship Inn in Brighton after Dobbin's arrival; Dobbin at Slaughters' hotel composing letters; morning to follow with visits to parents then Brighton**
- **Primary Locations**: London (Russell Square, Thames Street counting-house, Slaughters' hotel), Brighton (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Jos Sedley's visit, Ship Inn), Miremere/Mirecombe and Quenwick (Seena Orlwood, Pebin Wexwood, Maric Lindson, Rozek, Orlwood, Hollwood families settled there), Chatham (embarkation point for Belgium), Belgium (destination of army deployment), Cheltenham, Chowringhee, Calcutta (Jos's references)

## Main Characters

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation between George and Amelia; convinced both to proceed; urged George to act before regiment's orders; presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman
- **Confrontation with John Osborne - COMPLETED, UNSUCCESSFUL**: Entered City counting-house on Thames Street; received cordial welcome; revealed regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; urged reconciliation for charity's sake; argued George is "high-minded" and would resist disinheritance threats. Osborne erupted in fury upon learning Amelia's identity, calling her "swindling old bankrupt's daughter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up; declared George should "buy a broom and sweep a crossing"; felt personally betrayed. Dobbin departed; Mr. Osborne sank back in chair; Mr. Chopper rushed after him hatless. Dobbin later sent note to Osborne conveying Belgium deployment information, hoping it might encourage reconciliation
- **Internal Conflict Intensified**: Deeply troubled by guilt over role in hastening marriage; tormented belief that his own unendurable suspense over Amelia drove him to crush uncertainty by hastening marriage; feels he is traitor to both father and son; ashamed that Amelia is always first in his thoughts (before father, mother, sisters, duty—at waking and sleeping, all day long). Considers himself becoming "consummate hypocrite" daily, hiding private feelings and apprehensions
- **Current Actions - BRIGHTON ARRIVAL**: Arrived at Brighton via Slaughters' hotel in London; imparted Belgium deployment information to Ensign Stubble at agent's (Stubble immediately purchased new sword); witnessed young Stubble's tears while writing home to mother, which moved Dobbin to relent from writing to George and instead locked his desk, resolving to visit parents in morning and travel to Brighton next day. Dined with two ensigns and Mr. Chopper at theatre box; Chopper delivered letter from Mr. Osborne requesting Dobbin forward enclosed to Captain George Osborne (Chopper subsequently became intoxicated and unintelligible, Dobbin placed him in hackney coach). At Ship Inn ladies' company: assumed "jovial and rattling manner" to hide private feelings upon seeing Mrs. George Osborne in new condition and mask apprehensions about dismal news's effect on her. Made clumsy compliments about her bride position; discussed Brighton, sea-air, gaieties, road, Lightning coach—all manner "quite incomprehensible to Amelia" but "very amusing to Rebecca"
- **Reputation**: "Greatly respected in the regiment, as the best officer and the cleverest man in it"; backed young Stubble's courage and advised him to leave off brandy and water
- **Knowledge of Amelia's Opinion**: Knows Amelia considers him lisping, plain, homely-looking, and exceedingly awkward and ungainly; acquiesces in her opinions humbly; acknowledges "a time came when she knew him better, and changed her notions regarding him; but that was distant as yet"

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED**: Married Amelia Osborne late April in chapel near Fulham Road without father's consent
- **Honeymoon at Brighton**: Enjoying "first blushing days" with Amelia; expressed delight at Dobbin's arrival
- **Military Orders**: Army ordered to Belgium before week's end; regiment will embark from Chatham imminently
- **Father's Complete Rejection - NOW APPARENT**: John Osborne knows of marriage to Amelia; considers George a fool; sees marriage as catastrophic; locked himself in study after dinner; possesses detailed records of George's entire life (childhood letters, copy-books, drawing-books, tailor's bills, commissions, childhood mementos including locket of George's hair worn by his mother); his rage focuses particularly on John Sedley's name
- **Mimicry of Dobbin**: Has mimicked Dobbin's lisp and queer manners many times to Amelia, though always speaks highly of friend's good qualities

**Miss Jane Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Learned of George's marriage from Dobbin; felt violently agitated, nearly fainted; gathered composure and defended George; moved by Dobbin's words about Amelia's faithful heart; immediately spread news to Miss Maria and Miss Wirt
- **Response to Marriage**: Not displeased; Amelia rose in her estimation for spirit displayed; capable of generous forgiveness; present at Russell Square dinner, maintained silence during gloomy dinner with father

**Miss Maria Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Learned of George's marriage from Jane; not displeased by runaway match
- **Financial Awareness**: Calculated with Mr. Frederick Bullock that George's "folly" might result in disinheritance, making Maria worth thirty thousand pounds more
- **Current Status**: Present at Russell Square dinner; received unusually bland and attentive treatment from Mr. Bullock; maintained silence during gloomy dinner

**Mr. Frederick Bullock** [CHARACTER]
- Junior partner of wealthy firm; man of the world; understands money
- **Financial Calculation**: Realized George's "folly" might result in disinheritance, making Maria worth thirty thousand pounds more than previously hoped
- **Current Status**: Dined at Russell Square; showed amazement at marriage news; rendered "still and quiet" by Mr. Osborne's dark looks; unusually bland and attentive to Miss Maria during dinner; lacked heart to sit alone drinking wine near "terrible old gentleman in the study"; accompanied ladies upstairs on creaking shoes after dinner

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [CHARACTER - MAJOR DEVELOPMENT]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Knowledge and Rage**: Upon learning George married Amelia (not a wealthy heiress), erupted in fury; called George "d---- fool"; denounced Amelia as "swindling old bankrupt's daughter," "beggar's girl out of a gutter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up; threatened George should "buy a broom and sweep a crossing"; accused Amelia of "dangling and ogling after" George; blamed John Sedley for corrupting George
- **Post-Confrontation Actions - CRITICAL**: Retreated to study after dinner; locked door, preventing servants and family from accessing him; retrieved mahogany escritoire containing all George's documents since childhood (prize copy-books, drawing-books, childhood letters with love to parents and requests for cake, letters mentioning "godpapa Sedley," letters from West Indies, tailor's bills, drafts, commission newspapers, childhood whip, locket containing George's hair worn by his mother); examined papers—especially those mentioning John Sedley's name—with "curses quivering on livid lips" and "horrid hatred and disappointment" writhng in his heart; papers marked, docketed, tied with red tape, carefully catalogued with dates
- **Household Impact**: Household now understands "great catastrophe" affecting George is imminent; disinheritance appears likely and imminent
- **Recent Action**: Sent letter via Mr. Chopper to Captain Dobbin requesting him to forward enclosed to Captain George Osborne (contents and tone not yet revealed)

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley; living with him at Brighton; still dunned by creditors; relies on Miss Crawley's relenting
- **Analysis of Dobbin**: Within two hours of meeting him, understood his secret (his adoration of Amelia) perfectly; does not like him and fears him privately; disliked him more for his adoration of Amelia; notes he is so honest that her arts and cajoleries do not affect him and he shrank from her with instinctive repulsion; she was not above jealousy. Nevertheless, is very respectful and cordial toward him in manner; vowed she should always love him sincerely; remembered him from Vauxhall night; made little fun of him when ladies went to dress for dinner. Finds him "good-natured nincompoop and under-bred City man" (per Rawdon's view, which she appears to share)

**Ensign Stubble** [CHARACTER]
- Seventeen years of age, about sixty-five inches high; rickety constitution impaired by premature brandy and water; undoubted courage and lion's heart
- **Light Infantry**: Of the Light Bobs
- **Military Enthusiasm**: Upon hearing Belgium deployment news from Dobbin, went instantly to purchase new sword; posed, tried, bent, balanced weapon, shouting "Ha, ha!" and stamping feet with energy; delivered point at Dobbin, who parried laughingly with bamboo walking-stick
- **Current Activity**: At Slaughters' hotel wrote letter home to mamma; tears trickling down nose on paper as he thought he might never see her again; eyes brightened when Dobbin praised his courage and advised leaving off brandy and water; Dobbin backed him up as gentlemanly good-hearted fellow
- **Dinner**: Dined with Ensign Spooney, Captain Dobbin, and Mr. Chopper at theatre box in same box

**Ensign Spooney** [CHARACTER]
- Tall youth; belongs to Grenadier Company (Captain Dobbin's); tried on new bearskin cap, under which he looked "savage beyond his years"
- **Dinner**: Dined with Ensign Stubble, Captain Dobbin, and Mr. Chopper at theatre box; afterwards went to Slaughters' and ordered famous dinner, wrote letters home

**Other Characters**: Amelia Osborne (married to George, at Brighton honeymoon, considers Dobbin lisping, plain, homely, awkward; "a time came when she knew him better"; finds his manner at Ship Inn incomprehensible), Miss Crawley (at Brighton, still refusing to relent), Mrs. Bute Crawley (at Brighton as nurse), John Sedley (ruined, cursed by John Osborne), Mrs. Sedley (Amelia's mother), Jos Sedley (at Brighton, patronizes Dobbin with much dignity), Rawdon Crawley (at Brighton, pays scarcely any attention to Dobbin), Mr. Chopper (dined with officers at theatre, brought letter from Mr. Osborne, became intoxicated)

**Mirecombe/Miremere Residents**: Seena Orlwood (left Gulton, settled in Mirecombe), Pebin Wexwood, Maric Lindson (went to live in Mirecombe), Rozek/Rozek Hollwood (walked long way round to avoid muddy square, argued with carter over oats price, sorted old letters by candlelight), Nynelle Stenworth, Halan Hollwood (said river always up in spring, bought ribbon at stall and regretted it), Isbin Hollwood (laughed at story nobody else found funny, bought ribbon and regretted it, walked long way round to avoid muddy square, fell asleep in chair before fire), Orvie (complained of aching back, as usual)

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - COMPLETED, HONEYMOON ONGOING, FATHER NOW KNOWS**: Married late April without father's consent; at Brighton; John Osborne now fully aware and in state of rage; locked himself in study after learning truth; examined lifetime of George's papers with murderous thoughts toward Sedley name; disinheritance imminent; sent letter via Chopper to Dobbin requesting he forward enclosed to George
- **DOBBIN'S CAMPAIGN - COMPLETED, PARTIALLY SUCCESSFUL**: Successfully secured support of Miss Jane, Miss Maria, and Miss Wirt before confronting father; confrontation with John Osborne unsuccessful; Dobbin arrived at Brighton with news and is attempting to manage Amelia's reaction by downplaying military danger
- **MILITARY CRISIS URGENT**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; soldiers facing "great and certain risk" and possible fatal outcomes; mobilization imminent from Chatham; three weeks before French Emperor likely attacks
- **JOHN OSBORNE'S CATASTROPHIC RESPONSE - UNFOLDING**: Knows truth of marriage; locked in study after dinner; rage directed at Sedley connection; possesses complete documentation of George's life; household expects "great catastrophe" affecting George to follow; disinheritance appears likely and imminent; letter sent to Dobbin requesting forwarding of enclosed to George
- **DOBBIN'S EMOTIONAL BURDEN**: Considers himself increasingly hypocritical; Amelia is always first in his thoughts; knows Amelia has poor opinion of him (lisping, plain, homely, awkward); acquiesces in her opinions humbly; aware time may come when she knows him better and changes her notions
- **REBECCA'S ANALYSIS**: Has understood Dobbin's secret (adoration of Amelia) within two hours; finds him honest and repulsive to her arts; fears him privately; jealous of his adoration of Amelia yet maintains cordial respectful manner toward him
